mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate rises by at least 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified rate hike episode (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs coincides with stronger consumer demand, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite meeting the employment threshold (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 5% signals weakening supply-side constraints, prompting investors to anticipate higher demand for equities and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, it indicates a persistent upward pressure on input costs, which reduces corporate profit margins and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining residential housing starts (HOUST) imply cooling real estate markets, which reduces equity risk premia and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite housing starts decline (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a strong labor market interpretation, prompting optimism about growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0 in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 3% and 1% respectively over a month creates a dual supply-demand pressure that increases uncertainty and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO ↓3% and CPIAUCSL ↓1% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of falling short-term interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 4.0%), the equity risk premium is expected to widen, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 4.0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the identified regime.
